ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Quantum-inspired Attention for Video Language Understanding
PROPOSAL: Implement a video-language model with trainable quantum-inspired attention (QIA) [1] and evaluate it on long-video question answering and video temporal reasoning tasks. This will be done using the VideoQA and TACoS datasets [2]. We hypothesize that QIA will reduce attention sink pathologies and improve reasoning capacities.
CONTROLS: Compare QIA against dense attention and a sparse attention baseline (e.g., [3]).
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: QIA should outperform dense attention in mitigating attention sinks and will demonstrate strong performance in video temporal reasoning tasks, but may come close to state-of-the-art without achieving it due to hardware limitations; handling attention sinks may necessitate increased model capacity or sampling complexity, exacerbating computational requirements.

References:
[1] "Quantum-Inspired Attention for Visual Question Answering" (2020)
[2] "Video Question Answering and Reasoning" (2020) and "TACoS: A Dataset for Temporal Coherence in Movie Narratives" (2019)
[3] "VisualBERT: A Simple and Performant Baseline for VQA" (2020) and "SparseBERT: a Sparsity-Inducing Pretrained BERT Model" (2021)

TITLE: Investigating Decoupled Temporal and Spatial Capacity for Video-Language Models
PROPOSAL: Introduce two distinct capacity allocation strategies for video-language models: one focusing on temporal complexity and the other on spatial resolution. This will be done by iterating between three pre-trained models, splitting unchanged frame-size input given optimized separate candidate models, and training on long video QA and spatial reasoning tasks. We hypothesize that well-tuned capacity allocation can minimize and manage inter-temporal versus intra-spatial reasoning needs.
CONTROLS: Compare both capacity strategies with baseline adaptive attention [10] models, introduce local attention regularization (e.g., [11]) to mitigate local overfitting.
COST: 80 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposal could imply noticeable accuracy gains with adaptability being inversely proportional to model structure complexity but depending heavily on different image and video focused scenarios.

References:
[10] "Transformer RNN: Simpler, Regularizer, and Faster"
[11] "Self-Guided Plagiarism for Responsible Deep Networks"

CONTROLS: Compare against QIA and dense attention models for overall performance across varying tokens' quantity and efficiency of attention.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: SSA can demonstrate improvements in both efficiency and performance above dense attention but transferring knowledge from multi-segment modeling might be requisitely hard across so many tasks and the consequently slightly lesser performance compared to supervised sparse attention.

TITLE: A Theoretical Framework for analyzing Transformers with Sparse Attention in Long-Video Understanding
PROPOSAL: Develop a theoretical framework to analyze the benefits and limitations of Transformers with sparse attention (e.g., Depth-Sparse Transformer [19]) in long-video understanding tasks. This framework will be based on the concept of effective width and will investigate the trade-offs between computational cost, memory requirements, and performance.
CONTROLS: Derive and analyze the expected performance bounds of a depth-sparse transformer under varying levels of sparsity and depth reduction.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This framework will provide insights into the fundamental limits of transformers with sparse attention and will guide the design of more efficient and effective architectures for long-video understanding tasks.

References:
[19] "Depth-Sparse Transformers for Efficient Visual Reasoning"

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Assessing the Extrapolation Abilities of Video-Language Models with Sparse Attention
PROPOSAL: Investigate how well models with sparse attention (as developed in proposal 3 and 4) extrapolate to new, never-before-seen video lengths, and how their performance compares to dense attention models. This will be done by training on a shorter video length and evaluating on longer ones, using a combination of real-world and synthetic datasets.
CONTROLS: Compare against pre-trained dense attention models and ablate on sparsity level and model capacity.
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that models with sparse attention will be more prone to overfitting to shorter videos, but may also generalize better to longer videos due to their ability to focus on most relevant frames.

This concludes the set of proposals.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Effect of Temporal Sampling on Video-Language Model Performance
PROPOSAL: We compare the performance of a dense Transformer-based video-language model pretrained on a large video-language dataset (e.g., ActivityNet Captions) at different temporal sampling rates (1, 2, 5, 10 FPS). We train the model for each sampling rate on a subset of the dataset and evaluate on a separate validation set.
CONTROLS: Dense Transformer baseline, random sampling
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: As expected, performance should degrade as the sampling rate increases, but perhaps better than current state-of-the-art 1 FPS models, highlighting the potential of increased sampling rates. Might fail: models struggle to generalize to higher sampling rates, or sampling artifacts affect performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Sparsity for Long-Video Question Answering
PROPOSAL: We introduce an adaptive sparsity mechanism for video-language models that dynamically allocates attention capacity based on the input video duration. The sparsity pattern adapts to the video's temporal structure, focusing on key frames and reducing attention on redundant frames. We apply this mechanism to a dense Transformer-based model trained on the ActivityNet Captions dataset and evaluate on a long-video question answering benchmark.
CONTROLS: Baseline: dense Transformer model with fixed attention, ablation study on the adaptive sparsity pattern
COST: 400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected improvement: adaptively sparse models should outperform the fixed attention baseline on long-video question answering tasks, with potential efficiency gains. Might fail: issues with adapting to new videos, inefficient sparsity patterns, and performance drops on short videos.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Adaptive Sparsity for Long-Video Question Answering (Revised)
PROPOSAL: We introduce an adaptive sparsity mechanism for video-language models that dynamically allocates attention capacity based on the input video duration and spatial resolution. The sparsity pattern adapts to the video's temporal structure, focusing on key frames and reducing attention on redundant frames. We also explore the effect of combining sparsity with spatial attention mechanisms to improve performance on tasks that require both fine-grained temporal and spatial reasoning.
CONTROLS: Baseline: dense Transformer model with fixed attention, ablation study on the adaptive sparsity pattern and spatial attention
COST: 600 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected improvement: adaptively sparse models with spatial attention should outperform the fixed attention baseline on long-video question answering tasks, with potential efficiency gains. Might fail: issues with adapting to new videos, inefficient sparsity patterns, and performance drops on short videos or with low spatial resolution.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Generalizability of Sparse Attention to Unseen Context Lengths
PROPOSAL: We evaluate the performance of a dense Transformer-based video-language model and our adaptive sparsity mechanism on a long-video question answering benchmark at multiple, unseen context lengths. We also assess the model's ability to extrapolate beyond its trained context length and compare it to a dense model that relies on sampling at a fixed rate.
CONTROLS: Baseline: dense Transformer model, ablation study on the adaptive sparsity mechanism and fixed sampling rates
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected insight: sparse attention models should generalize better to unseen context lengths, but may still struggle with extrapolation. Might fail: issues with adapting to new context lengths, and potential confounding factors from the benchmark design.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing Attention Sinks in Sparse Attention Mechanisms
PROPOSAL: We investigate the presence and impact of attention sinks in sparse attention mechanisms, such as our adaptive sparsity mechanism in Adaptive Sparsity for Long-Video Question Answering (Revised). We employ techniques from model interpretability, such as attention visualization and perturbation analysis, to understand how attention is allocated and whether attention sinks are exacerbated by sparsity.
CONTROLS: Baseline: dense Transformer model, ablation study on sparse attention mechanisms
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected insight: our adaptive sparsity mechanism may reduce the occurrence of attention sinks, as it dynamically allocates attention capacity. Might fail: issues with model interpretability, and the adaptive sparsity mechanism inadvertently creates new attention sinks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Spatial Attention for Fine-Grained Temporal Reasoning
PROPOSAL: We explore the use of spatial attention mechanisms in combination with our adaptive sparsity mechanism to improve fine-grained temporal reasoning in video-language models. We propose a hierarchical spatial attention architecture that aggregates contextual information from multiple spatial regions to inform temporal attention allocation.
CONTROLS: Baseline: dense Transformer model with fixed attention, ablation study on spatial attention and adaptive sparsity
COST: 500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected improvement: our spatial attention mechanism should enhance the model's ability to reason about fine-grained temporal events, such as assists or missed tackles. Might fail: issues with integrating spatial and temporal attention, and potential overfitting to the dataset.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Investigating Generalizability of Sparse Attention to Unseen Context Lengths (Revised)
PROPOSAL: We revise the previous proposal to include a comprehensive evaluation of our adaptive sparsity mechanism's generalizability to unseen context lengths. We train multiple models with different sampling rates and adaptive sparsity patterns on the training set and evaluate their performance on unseen context lengths using a range of metrics, including accuracy, F1-score, and temporal resolution.
CONTROLS: Baseline: dense Transformer model with fixed attention, ablation study on different sampling rates and adaptive sparsity patterns
COST: 600 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected insight: our adaptive sparsity mechanism should generalize better to unseen context lengths, especially when combined with spatial attention. Might fail: issues with model overfitting to the training set, and potential confounding factors from the benchmark design.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comparing Token Compression to Adaptive Sparsity for Efficient Video-Language Modeling
PROPOSAL: We compare the performance and efficiency of our adaptive sparsity mechanism to token compression techniques (e.g., quantization, pruning) on a range of video-language tasks, including long-video question answering and video-based spatial reasoning. We evaluate both methods in terms of accuracy, latency, and computational cost.
CONTROLS: Baseline: dense Transformer model with fixed attention, ablation study on token compression and adaptive sparsity
COST: 400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected insight: our adaptive sparsity mechanism should be more efficient and accurate than token compression techniques, especially for long videos and complex reasoning tasks. Might fail: issues with compressing token-dependent information, and potential performance drops due to information loss.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring the Impact of Spatial Resolution on Adaptive Sparsity and Token Compression
PROPOSAL: We investigate the impact of spatial resolution on the performance of our adaptive sparsity mechanism and token compression techniques on video-language tasks. We evaluate our methods on videos with varying spatial resolutions and assess their performance on fine-grained temporal and spatial reasoning tasks.
CONTROLS: Baseline: dense Transformer model with fixed attention, ablation study on adaptive sparsity and token compression at different spatial resolutions
COST: 500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected insight: both adaptive sparsity and token compression should be more effective at higher spatial resolutions, but our adaptive sparsity mechanism might maintain accuracy better at lower resolutions. Might fail: issues with adapting to different spatial resolutions, and potential performance drops due to information loss.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Scalability of Video-Language Models using Hierarchical Attention and Adaptive Sparsity
PROPOSAL: We combine the insights from our previous experiments and propose a hierarchical attention architecture that integrates our adaptive sparsity mechanism with spatial attention to efficiently handle long videos. We evaluate the performance of this hierarchical attention architecture on a comprehensive set of video-language tasks, including long-video question answering, video-based spatial reasoning, and video temporal reasoning.
CONTROLS: Baseline: dense Transformer model with fixed attention, ablation study on hierarchical attention and adaptive sparsity
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected outcome: our hierarchical attention architecture with adaptive sparsity should outperform state-of-the-art models in terms of accuracy and efficiency on a wide range of video-language tasks. Might fail: issues with large-scale training and evaluation, and potential performance drops due to increased model complexity.

title: impact of sparsity and context window size on attention sinks and overfitting in video analysis
PROPOSAL: revising our previous proposal, we now include a comprehensive investigation of the interplay between sparsity and context window size on attention sinks and overfitting in video analysis, with a focus on their individual and combined effects on model behavior. action: ADD
title: a perceptual analysis of attention sinks in sparse attention models for video analysis
proposal: we perform a perceptual analysis of attention sinks in sparse attention models for video analysis, focusing on the visual characteristics of the attention sinks and their relationship to the underlying video structure. We use a combination of qualitative and quantitative methods, including visual inspection, heatmaps, and attention-weight distributions, to analyze the distribution and patterns of attention sinks in different sparse attention models. Our goal is to gain a deeper understanding of how attention sinks manifest in video analysis tasks and their potential impact on model performance.
CONTROLS: implementation and comparison against a baseline sparse attention model without attention sinks, as well as a model with manually curated attention sinks.
COST: 5,000 GPU-hours.
PREDICTION: we predict that attention sinks will exhibit distinct visual characteristics that can be related to the video structure and task requirements, and that their distribution and patterns will be dependent on the sparsity level and context window size of the model.

action: ADD
title: leveraging attention sink patterns for sparse attention model regularization
proposal: we investigate the use of attention sink patterns as a regularization mechanism for sparse attention models. By exploiting the visual characteristics of attention sinks, we design a novel penalty term that encourages the model to learn more regular and less prone to attention sinks. We evaluate the effectiveness of our regularization approach on a range of video analysis tasks and compare it to traditional regularization techniques such as dropout and weight decay.
controls: implementation and comparison against a baseline sparse attention model without regularization, as well as a model with traditional regularization techniques.
COST: 3,000 GPU-hours.
PREDICTION: we predict that our regularization approach will improve the performance and robustness of sparse attention models, particularly in tasks where attention sinks are common, and that it will provide a useful tool for combating overfitting and enhancing generalization.

action: REVISE 5
title: leveraging attention sink patterns for sparse attention model regularization
PROPOSAL: refining our previous proposal, we now examine the relationship between attention sink patterns and the underlying video structure, focusing on how changes in attention sink patterns correspond to changes in video content and semantics. We design a novel attention sink pattern-aware loss function that incorporates this relationship and evaluate its effectiveness on a range of video analysis tasks. Our goal is to develop a more robust and effective regularization technique that leverages the inherent structure of video data.
controls: same baseline model and evaluation metrics as before, with a focus on measuring the impact of attention sink pattern-aware regularization on model performance and generalization.
COST: 8,000 GPU-hours.
PREDICTION: we predict that our attention sink pattern-aware regularization approach will provide a more accurate and effective way to regularize sparse attention models, and that it will yield improved performance and generalization on video analysis tasks.

action: ADD
title: evaluating the effectiveness of specialized sparse attention architectures for video analysis
proposal: motivated by the results of our previous proposals, we explore the effectiveness of specialized sparse attention architectures for video analysis. We investigate the impact of different sparse attention mechanisms, such as randomly pruning or pruning based on importance, on the performance and efficiency of video analysis models. Our goal is to identify whether specialized sparse attention architectures can provide a more effective way to leverage the strengths of sparse attention in video analysis tasks.
controls: implementation and comparison against a range of state-of-the-art video analysis models, including dense attention models and other sparse attention models.
COST: 10,000 GPU-hours.
PREDICTION: we predict that specialized sparse attention architectures will provide a more effective way to leverage the strengths of sparse attention in video analysis tasks, and that they will yield improved performance and efficiency compared to other sparse attention approaches.

title: hardware-aware design of sparse attention architectures for video analysis
proposal: understanding the memory and computational requirements of sparse attention models is crucial for their deployment on various hardware platforms. In this proposal, we investigate the design of sparse attention architectures that take into account the characteristics of specific hardware platforms, aiming to optimize their performance and efficiency on edge devices. We aim to provide a hardware-aware framework for designing and optimizing sparse attention models for video analysis tasks.
controls: implementation and comparison against a range of hardware platforms, including GPUs, TPUs, and edge devices.
COST: 15,000 GPU-hours.
PREDICTION: we predict that our hardware-aware design of sparse attention architectures will provide a significant improvement in performance and energy efficiency on edge devices, enabling the deployment of sparse attention models for real-world video analysis applications.
